key_insight: OrionMoE-Small improves tabular in-context learning by using dataset-conditioned sparse mixture-of-experts routing on top of a dual-axis Transformer, enabling adaptive computation without task-specific fine-tuning.
engineering_relevance: The model offers a compact, scalable alternative to dense tabular foundation models, especially for heterogeneous, small-context, and high-dimensional datasets.
method: Uses a dual-axis Transformer with distribution-aware feature representations.
Activates experts sparsely along the feature axis using routing informed by feature and dataset context.
Pretrains only on synthetic classification tasks from a structured causal prior, then predicts new tabular samples in-context.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports competitive results across multiple tabular benchmarks, with particularly strong performance on small-context and high-dimensional datasets, plus improved behavior under class imbalance.
watch_item: Because the model is pretrained entirely on synthetic tasks, real-world generalization may depend on how well the synthetic causal prior matches target tabular domains.
paper_title: OrionMoE-v1.0: A Mixture-of-Experts Foundation Model for Tabular In-Context Learning
